Definition: a whistling (in scorn); by analogy, a piping
BiblicalUsage: Deborah asks why Reuben stayed among the sheepfolds to hear the piping of the flocks, and Jeremiah says the land will become a hissing forever.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the same whistling can be a shepherd's tune or a scornful hiss, and the difference is which side of the battle I stand on.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
